response.title: Harden labnb slice monitor with break conditions and exit codes
response.body:
## Summary

Turns `monitor_slice.py check` into a real loop circuit-breaker so a slice can be cut short on more than just elapsed time.

- **Exit-code contract:** `check` exits non-zero (default `4`) on a break decision, so `while monitor_slice.py check ...; do run_iteration; done` stops on its own. `--exit-zero` keeps the legacy always-0 behavior.
- **Budget hardening:** `--reserve-seconds` breaks while slack remains for verify/log/summary; `--warn-fraction` (default 0.8) emits an advisory `warn` before the cap.
- **Engineering signals:** pace projection breaks when another iteration at the recent cadence won't fit the remaining loop budget (`--no-pace` to disable); `--stall-seconds` breaks on no new `results.tsv` row; `--usage-file` + `--max-rss-bytes`/`--max-pmem` break on runaway memory read from a con/duct log (live `usage.jsonl` totals or post-run `info.json`).
- **Correctness signals:** `--max-failures` breaks after N consecutive failed/crashed iterations.
- **Validity signals:** `--patience` breaks on a no-improvement plateau (using the recorded `direction`); `--metric-guardrail` breaks when the latest metric crosses a hard bound the wrong way.

When several trip at once, **correctness > budget > engineering > validity** selects the terminal status (`crashed` / `budget_exhausted` / `stopped`). The decision, all signals, and diagnostics are recorded in the provenance state snapshot. All diagnostics are derived from `results.tsv` + provenance — no new mutable state file.

## Review fixes (this PR also addresses a skills review)
- **Slice scoping:** stall age, pace cadence, and consecutive-failure counts are scoped to the current slice (rows at/after `slice_started_at`), so a resumed/multi-slice experiment is not penalized for a prior slice. No-improvement / `--patience` is intentionally cumulative and documented as such.
- **Script paths:** `labnb` and every `labnb-*` companion now document that helper script paths resolve relative to the installed skill directory (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/labnb/scripts/`), not the repo layout.
- **Docs:** a break does not auto-close the slice (call `finish`); `--patience` treats ties as a plateau.
- **Validator:** `validate_skills.py` parses SKILL.md frontmatter with PyYAML when available, falling back to the hand-rolled parser.

## Validation
- 65 tests pass, including `tests/test_monitor_slice.py` (each break class, priority ordering, slice scoping, pace/usage parsing, exit-code wiring); the two budget tests assert the new exit `4`.
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all skills valid.

## Remaining known limitation
- Enforcement is cooperative: `check` reports and exits non-zero but does not kill a running process.

Make neuroscience NER taxonomy suggested rather than closed

What

Reframes the label taxonomy in skills/structsense-skills/prompts/extractor-ner-neuroscience.md from a strict closed list into a set of suggested labels. The extractor is now encouraged to assign the most appropriate label to each entity, coining a concise descriptive label when none of the suggested ones fits well.

Why

The previous instruction ("use these exactly; do NOT invent others") forced every entity into one of the predefined labels or into the catch-all Other. For neuroscience text spanning behavior, systems, cellular, molecular, and computational scales, this meant genuine entities that didn't match the list got mislabeled or dumped into Other, losing information. Treating the taxonomy as guidance preserves consistency for common types while letting the model capture entities the fixed list doesn't anticipate.

response.title: Add orcd skill for MIT ORCD remote execution
response.body:
Connects `orcd-login.mit.edu` (Slurm cluster `eofe7`, Engaging) as a remote execution environment and packages what it takes to use it reliably from Claude Code / Cowork / Science.

## Why a skill rather than a README

Four things about ORCD are easy to get wrong and cost hours each time:

1. **SSH auth is two-factor even with a key**, and the failure message points at the wrong cause.
2. **Entitlements are per-person and invisible.** Partition access is gated by Unix group membership, so two people in the same lab get different answers and nothing can be hardcoded.
3. **Storage tiers differ by ~10x in speed**, and the slowest one (`$HOME`) is the default working directory.
4. **The configuration changes underneath you** — partitions retired, QOS ceilings retuned, GPU models swapped.

## Discovery, not hardcoding

Partition access comes from `AllowGroups`; per-user ceilings come from a QOS each partition attaches automatically. Neither is guessable, so the scripts ask the cluster at runtime:

- `scontrol show partition` for partitions and their gates — note `PrivateData=none` here, so this lists partitions regardless of access and **cannot** be used as an entitlement list.
- `sbatch --test-only` as the authoritative yes/no. It queues nothing, and it also reports **estimated start time**, which turns partition choice into a measurement.
- `sacctmgr show qos` for the ceilings that actually bind, distinguishing `MaxTRESPU` (yours alone) from `GrpTRES` (**one pool shared with the whole group**, so a colleague's job can block yours).
- GPU inventory from each partition's `TRES` string. Summing `sinfo` output instead undercounts badly, because `sinfo` collapses identically configured nodes onto one line.

## Config drift is captured, not discovered the hard way

`orcd_snapshot.py` emits a structured JSON snapshot of Slurm config, partitions, QOS ceilings, entitlements, quotas, and node shapes, and diffs it against a saved baseline. Diffs are keyed by content rather than list index so reordering is not reported as change, and each finding is annotated with why it matters (`"a --gres model may no longer exist"`). `--diff` exits 2 on change, so it works from cron or CI.

## Findings encoded in the scripts and docs

**SSH requires `publickey` AND `keyboard-interactive` (Duo).** The key alone leaves the session at "partial success"; Duo then answers the second stage, usually with zero prompts. So setting `BatchMode=yes` **always** fails with `Permission denied (keyboard-interactive)` — which reads like a rejected key, and sends people off replacing keys that were fine. Connection multiplexing (`ControlMaster` + `ControlPersist 12h`) is what keeps later calls non-interactive.

**Never pass `--qos`.** Most associations permit only `normal`, so naming a partition's own QOS fails with `Invalid qos specification`. Choose the partition; the QOS follows.

**Three job-count ceilings stack, and the smallest wins:** association `MaxSubmit` (one limit across *every* partition, and the one people miss because it never appears in `scontrol show partition`), partition QOS `MaxSubmitPU`, and `MaxArraySize`. Array tasks each count as a submitted job, so an oversized array is refused with `QOSMaxSubmitJobPerUserLimit` — and **`-a 0-999%50` is refused identically**, because `%K` caps concurrent *running* tasks, not submitted ones. Bisection in two partitions with very different caps shows the largest accepted array is **`MaxSubmitPU + 1`** (449 where the cap is 448, 5 where it is 4). The snapshot derives this per partition so it survives a QOS retune.

**Preemptable partitions are extra capacity, not worse capacity.** `mit_preemptable` spans nearly the whole cluster with GPU models available nowhere else, and is free to use whenever work can be interrupted. The requeue pattern is documented including the detail that decides whether it works: the signal handler must **exit non-zero**, or Slurm treats the job as finished and never requeues it.

## Storage

Tier is encoded in group names (`orcd_rg_<server>_<owner>`): `fstor*` is flash over NFS-over-RDMA, `hstor*` capacity disk, `core*` archive. Measured on an H100 node (1 GiB `dd`, plus 500 small-file creation):

| Tier | Write | Read | 500 files |
|---|---|---|---|
| bcs flash scratch | ~1000 MB/s | ~2900 MB/s | 0.13 s |
| `/orcd/compute/bcs/001` (flash) | 232 MB/s | 3300 MB/s | **3.19 s** |
| `/home` | 222 MB/s | 1300 MB/s | 0.78 s |

`/orcd/compute/bcs/001` has excellent reads but ~25x worse metadata than scratch, so it is for reading shared datasets rather than writing many small files. Node-local `/scratch` (3.5 TB) exists on some nodes but **not** on the bcs H100 nodes, while Slurm reports `TmpDisk=0` everywhere — so it must be probed, not assumed. These are single samples on a busy shared cluster; the docs present them as indicative, not constants.

**Per-user quotas come from `~/orcd/.quota`**, refreshed daily by ORCD. That report is the only place these limits appear — `df` shows the whole shared filesystem, so it reports hundreds of free TB in a space capped at 1 TB. Every user gets 200 GB in `$HOME` plus **1 TB flash scratch and 1 TB pool inside their home directory**. The file-count columns matter as much as the space columns: `HOME` and `SCRATCH` each carry a **1 M inode limit**, reached by one unpacked dataset at a few percent of the space quota, surfacing as a disk-full error against a quota that looks fine.

**Bug fixed during review of my own first pass:** per-user scratch is sharded across `/orcd/scratch/orcd/<NNN>` and the shard differs per user, so the hardcoded `001` was simply wrong for this account (`013`). Personal spaces are now resolved through the root-managed `~/orcd` symlinks, which is the only reliable way to find them.

**Two ways to hang a script here:** bare `df -h` blocks on unresponsive network mounts (it hit a 120s timeout during development), so the scripts read `/proc/mounts` and size paths individually under `timeout`; and `/orcd` is autofs, so listing a parent is not an inventory — project trees are found by enumerating the LDAP automount maps.

## Contents

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `orcd_doctor.py` | Verify access; route to the right remedy on failure. `--fix` writes SSH config |
| `orcd_resources.py` | Usable partitions, GPU models, QOS ceilings, live free capacity |
| `orcd_storage.py` | Writable storage by tier and speed, quotas. `--setup` creates per-user dirs |
| `orcd_submit.py` | Plan, submit, track; auto-selects partition by start time |
| `orcd_snapshot.py` | Structured config summary; `--save` a baseline, `--diff` to see drift |
| `orcd_common.py` | Shared SSH plumbing (multiplexing, base64 payloads, error mapping) |

Plus `references/setup.md`, `references/slurm.md`, `references/storage.md`. All scripts are stdlib-only Python 3, run locally over one multiplexed SSH connection, and accept `--host`; the data-gathering ones accept `--json`.

## Onboarding a new group member

ORCD accepts no password over SSH, so the key must be installed via the OnDemand portal (which does support Duo): sign in at https://orcd-ood.mit.edu/, use **Clusters → Shell Access**, append the public key to `authorized_keys`, then `orcd_doctor.py --fix` locally. The doctor prints this walkthrough itself when it detects the key is missing, and reports a missing Slurm association or `orcd_rg_*` groups as warnings — those need an email to orcd-help@mit.edu, not a config change.

## Verification

- Repo validator passes (9/9 skills); all 76 unit tests pass.
- `orcd_doctor.py` passes against the live cluster, and correctly fails with the right remedy on bad-DNS and bad-alias paths (exit 1). It also correctly diagnosed a genuine mid-session Duo expiry during development.
- Real GPU job submitted end-to-end: ran on `node1702`, got an H100 80GB, exit 0.
- Array limits established by bisection against the live scheduler, not assumed.
- `orcd_snapshot.py` verified both ways: clean diff on an unchanged cluster (exit 0), and against a deliberately mutated baseline covering lost partition access, a retired partition, a dropped GPU model, tightened ceilings, and a removed storage group — all detected and correctly explained (exit 2).
- `orcd_storage.py --setup` is idempotent.
- Installed copy matches the repo byte-for-byte; all probe artifacts cleaned off the cluster.

response.title: orcd-remote: manage uv in cluster home; gate profile edits on user approval
response.body:
## Summary

Updates the `orcd-remote` skill to manage `uv` in the cluster home directory, enforce user approval for any shell-profile change, and warn about cloud agent environments when asking for an SSH key to be installed.

### uv in the cluster `$HOME` (new `scripts/orcd_uv.py`)

- **Check**: reports whether `~/.local/bin/uv` exists on the cluster and its version, whether `uv` resolves on PATH for a fresh non-interactive SSH command, and which profiles already reference `~/.local/bin`. Supports `--json` and `--host` like the other scripts.
- **Install/upgrade** (`--install`): runs the official standalone installer pinned to `UV_INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin` with `UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` (so the installer can never edit startup files); upgrades an existing install via `uv self update`, surfacing the failure when uv was installed some other way (pip/conda/module).
- **PATH** (`--add-to-path`): appends `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to a chosen profile — but only past an approval gate (below). Idempotent, writes a `.orcd-uv.bak` backup first, and re-verifies over a fresh connection afterwards, reporting honestly when an interactivity guard in `~/.bashrc` keeps the line from reaching non-interactive shells.

### Profile changes require explicit user approval

- `--add-to-path` prints the exact file and line, then proceeds only after a typed `yes` on a TTY or an explicit `--user-approved` flag; in a non-interactive run without the flag it refuses and exits non-zero. Docs state agents must ask the user before passing the flag.
- The rule is documented in `SKILL.md` and `references/setup.md` as covering `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, and `~/.profile`, whether edited directly or by an installer.
- Scripts and sbatch jobs are steered to the absolute path `$HOME/.local/bin/uv` so nothing depends on the profile edit; docs also point uv caches/venvs at flash scratch to protect the 1 M inode quota.

### Doctor integration

- `orcd_doctor.py` now includes uv in its cluster sanity checks: `PASS` with the version, or a `WARN` pointing at `orcd_uv.py --install` when missing (access still counts as working).

### Cloud-environment note in the SSH key walkthrough

- `print_key_instructions` (and `references/setup.md` / `SKILL.md`) now note that when the session runs in a cloud or remote agent environment (Claude Code on the web, CI, devcontainer), the key pair lives in that ephemeral environment and installing it grants the environment access to the ORCD account — so get the owner's explicit OK, use a dedicated key with an identifying comment, remove it from `authorized_keys` when the environment is retired, and never copy private keys out of the container.

### TCP port-22 probe in the doctor (found by live-testing from a cloud container)

- Running the setup flow for real from a cloud agent container (HTTPS-only egress) showed the doctor misreading a blocked port 22 as an auth failure and prescribing key/Duo fixes that cannot help. The doctor now probes TCP 22 after DNS and before any ssh attempt; on failure it reports `port 22 is blocked`, prints an egress-specific remedy (cloud network policy, VPN), and skips the key-install walkthrough. Troubleshooting rows added to `SKILL.md` and `setup.md`.

### CI fix (pre-existing on `main`)

- Renamed `skills/brainkb_skills/` to `skills/brainkb/` to match its frontmatter `name: brainkb`. The format validator has been failing on `main` since the skill landed; this keeps the skill's trigger name intact and no other file referenced the old path.

### Docs kept in sync

- `SKILL.md`: new "Python on the cluster: uv in `$HOME`" section, scripts table, troubleshooting rows, frontmatter description.
- `references/setup.md`: cloud-environment note in the key steps, blocked-egress troubleshooting row, and a "Python tooling: uv in the cluster home" section.
- `references/slurm.md`: Software section points at `orcd_uv.py`.

## Testing

- `py_compile` on the new and changed scripts.
- Exercised `orcd_uv.py` end-to-end against a sandboxed fake `$HOME` (stubbed `run_remote` executing the generated bash payloads): 18/18 checks pass — missing-uv exit code, check parsing, refusal without approval (no file touched), approved append + backup + idempotency, add-to-path refusal when uv missing, self-update failure surfacing, JSON output.
- Live-ran the doctor from a cloud container with no ssh client, no key, and blocked port 22: each precondition fails in dependency order with the intended remedy, including the new cloud-environment note and the new blocked-egress diagnosis; verified the port-22 probe passes against a live listener and falls through to the normal checks.
- Repo checks locally: `scripts/validate_skills.py` — all 11 skills valid; `tests/` — 76/76 pass.

Cluster-side behavior (actual install over SSH) not exercised — this environment's network policy blocks SSH egress, which is what motivated the port-probe commit.

response.title: orcd-remote: add --sandbox-setup for authorizing an internet-connected sandbox
response.body:
## Summary

When the orcd-remote skill runs in a sandbox that has internet access (SSH egress to port 22 works), the client side of getting authorized can be fully automated. The previous walkthrough was laptop-shaped — clipboard copies via `pbcopy`/`xclip`, "back on your laptop" verification — and had no path for "the agent's own environment needs authorization".

### New: `orcd_doctor.py --sandbox-setup`

- **Verifies egress first** (DNS + the existing `tcp port 22` probe) — no key is minted for a network that can never present it. On blocked egress it prints the standard remedy, plus where this environment's public key lives in case the owner wants to pre-authorize anyway (with the caveat that a future sandbox carries a different key).
- **Mints a dedicated key if the sandbox has none**: `ed25519`, identifying `orcd-sandbox-<user>-<date>` comment, empty passphrase (the headless/ephemeral/revocable trade-off the cloud-environment notes already accept).
- **Prints two ready-to-paste commands for the account owner**: one appending the public key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on ORCD (run in the portal shell or any authorized SSH session), and one revoking it later by comment tag. The owner running the append command *is* the authorization step — an agent never adds the key itself.
- Points at `orcd_doctor.py --fix` as the follow-up that verifies the connection and writes the ssh config.

### Refactor

- The blocked-egress remedy moved from an inline print in `main()` into a shared `egress_blocked_message()` helper used by both the normal doctor path and sandbox setup.

### Docs

- `SKILL.md`: the cloud-agent note now includes the sandbox flow.
- `references/setup.md`: new "Sandbox with SSH egress" subsection under the cloud-environment block, including the passphrase trade-off and the never-add-the-key-yourself rule.
- The doctor's key-install walkthrough points at `--sandbox-setup`.

## Testing

- Blocked egress (live, from a cloud container with HTTPS-only policy): refuses with the remedy plus the pre-authorize note, exit 1.
- Open egress (loopback listener on :22): with an existing key — prints the authorize command containing the exact pubkey, revoke command, and `--fix` follow-up, exit 0; with a fresh `HOME` — generates the key with the `orcd-sandbox-<user>-<date>` comment and prints both commands, exit 0.
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all 11 skills valid; `tests/`: 76/76 pass.

response.title: orcd-remote: fix 14 script defects, correct docs, add login-node/scratch conventions, compress for tokens
response.body:
## Summary

Outcome of a full review of the `orcd-remote` skill (every doc and script read, plus an independent adversarial pass over the scripts). Three commits:

### 1. Script fixes (14 confirmed defects) + parser tests

| Script | Defect | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orcd_snapshot.py` | node shapes split on the `\|` inside the shape → recorded `{cpu_count: memory}`; fleet changes never diffed | `rpartition` off the trailing count |
| `orcd_snapshot.py` | 1% numeric tolerance (for rendered quota jitter) also hid integer changes: node counts, `MaxSubmitPU`, GPU totals | integers compare exactly |
| `orcd_storage.py --setup` | appended `/<user>` to the already-per-user `~/orcd/scratch` target → `<user>/<user>`; new dirs left at default umask | skip ORCD-provisioned personal targets; `chmod o-rwx`; report mode |
| `orcd_storage.py` | probe bounded `df` but not `test -e`/`-w` → one stale mount still hung the whole inventory | all touches under `timeout`; stale paths reported, not fatal |
| `orcd_storage.py` | untouched `/orcd/pool` classified `other`, dropping from "Where to put what" | `/orcd/pool/` → capacity |
| `orcd_storage.py` | quota label rendered `0T` below 1 TiB | reuse the size string |
| `orcd_resources.py --idle` | `sinfo`'s `*` on the default partition never matched `scontrol`'s name → its idle GPUs hidden; untyped GPUs dropped | strip `*`; shared `gpu_counts()` handles untyped |
| `orcd_resources.py` | dead `tres_summary()` | removed |
| `orcd_doctor.py` | regex config detection matched `Host orcd-login.mit.edu` for alias `orcd`, missed `Host *` BatchMode and `Include`d files | `ssh -G` (merges Include/Match/wildcards) |
| `orcd_doctor.py --fix` | empty `$USER` wrote a bare `User` line → ssh refuses its config for every host | refused with a clear error |
| `orcd_doctor.py` | reachable-without-alias exited 0 and pointed at scripts that default to the alias | explicit `--fix` hint |
| `orcd_doctor.py` | first-found key forced with `IdentitiesOnly` | `--identity <path>` |
| `orcd_common.py` | ssh exit 255 with `check=False` returned `""` → empty storage table, and `--plan` silently lost its `EXCEEDS` cross-check | 255 always raises |
| `orcd_common.py` | errors from `2>&1` commands lost (stderr empty) | include stdout tail |
| `orcd_submit.py` | no way to move job cwd off `$HOME` | `--chdir` (sbatch `-D`) |

`tests/test_orcd_parsers.py` (20 tests) exercises all of the above against recorded-style fixtures with the cluster stubbed; `ssh -G` tests skip if no ssh client.

### 2. Documentation corrections + new conventions

- **Contradictions fixed**: the array recipe was the exact command the same file shows being refused (array > `MaxSubmitPU`); the training recipe's relative `-o logs/…` fails at job start when submitted from `$HOME` through this skill (now absolute `-D`/`-o`, and the symptom is in the troubleshooting table); storage.md claimed capacity differs from flash on metadata while its own table shows them equal — the tiers to avoid are `$HOME` and the flash *project* tier; passphrase keys need `ssh-agent` since the scripts close stdin; `%N`/`%K` unified.
- **Login nodes are for orchestration, not work**: every `ssh orcd '<cmd>'` lands on a login node, so the documented default for real work is a one-shot `srun -p mit_quicktest -t 15 …`, escalating to `ou_*_high`/`mit_normal`, with `mit_data_transfer` for copies.
- **Two flash scratches, two purposes**: personal `~/orcd/scratch` (1 TB, 1 M inodes) for Python environments and `UV_CACHE_DIR`; group `/orcd/scratch/bcs/<NNN>/<user>` for runs. **Group scratch dirs are group-readable and closed to everyone outside the group**: `--setup` applies `chmod o-rwx`, job scripts use `umask 027`. Documented in `storage.md`, `sensein.md`, `sensein.json` (printed by `orcd_storage.py`).

### 3. Token economy

`SKILL.md` — the part every triggered session pays for — rewritten from 425 lines / 3,594 words to **210 lines / 1,692 words**, keeping every rule and pointing at `references/` for the reasoning; frontmatter description trimmed to triggers plus a one-line capability summary (591 chars). Script stdout paragraphs that duplicated the references cut to one or two lines each.

## Testing

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 96/96 (76 existing + 20 new).
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all 11 skills valid.
- Live smoke from this cloud container (blocked egress): `orcd_doctor.py --sandbox-setup` still diagnoses correctly with the compressed text; the earlier end-to-end uv flow test still passes.

response.title: orcd-remote: seven field traps, and how to get code onto the cluster
response.body:
Findings from running a 388-recording campaign across ten Slurm array jobs on Engaging, plus several smaller runs. Each cost real time to diagnose once, and none was guessable from the docs as they stand.

## What changed

**New `references/code.md` — getting code onto the cluster.** Login nodes carry no GitHub credentials, no agent forwarding, and no accepted GitHub host key, so `git fetch` fails there by default. Two paths: a read-only **deploy key** generated on the cluster into a dedicated file (with `CheckHostIP no` for `github.com`, which removes the stale-IP host-key trap permanently), or `git bundle` — one credential-free file with the exact commit range (path resolved once locally; scp's SFTP mode never expands variables). Plus: echo the resolved commit into job output; reuse checkouts and venvs (a fresh `uv sync` costs tens of thousands of inodes). SKILL.md carries the rule and a pointer.

**`orcd_doctor.py` — `git over ssh (cluster)` check.** One strict, read-only `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -T git@github.com` probe from the login node, classified by `classify_git()` into: authenticated / stale IP-keyed host key (names the offending IP and file) / host key not accepted / no key registered / no answer. The doctor never accepts a host key on the user's behalf. Tested against the recorded GitHub messages.

**Eight troubleshooting rows** (SKILL.md), one clause per cell:

- `git` under BatchMode fails on a login node but works by hand — stale IP-keyed GitHub host key, intermittent with DNS.
- `git` on a login node: `Permission denied (publickey)` — no cluster-side key; local keys do not forward.
- An array runs N at a time though `%K` allows more — `QOSGrpGRES`, the group's concurrent-GPU pool (`LIMIT: GROUP` in `orcd_resources.py`).
- `sacct` says `COMPLETED` but nothing was produced — a step failed and the wrapper exited 0; `set -eo pipefail`.
- Model load fails on a missing weight file — incomplete snapshot in a shared HF cache; load one model in `mit_quicktest` before a long array.
- Your agent is killed while the job runs on — a long foreground wait tripped a stall watchdog; poll with short separate checks.
- A task finishes, then idles ~18 min before exiting — Python 3.12.0 only (`multiprocess` `ResourceTracker.__del__`, `RLock._recursion_count` missing); pin ≥ 3.12.1.
- `rsync` fails on a remote path containing `(` or `)` — quote for the remote shell, or tar over ssh.

**sensein reference**: a shared HF cache can hold an incomplete snapshot that passes every check short of loading.

**Verbiage pass over the references** (`setup.md`, `slurm.md`, `storage.md`, `sensein.md`): rules SKILL.md already states and narrative around facts removed; every command, number and table kept. Reference words 7,110 → 4,745 including the new `code.md`.

## Testing

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: all pass (3 new `classify_git` tests).
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all 11 skills valid; every doc link resolves.

response.title: orcd-remote: catch jobs held behind a maintenance reservation
response.body:
## The trap

A reservation does not refuse a job. When the requested time limit cannot finish before the window opens, Slurm **holds** the job until the window *ends*: state `PENDING`, reason `ReqNodeNotAvail, Reserved for maintenance`. Nothing distinguishes that from ordinary queue time. ORCD runs a monthly cluster-wide maintenance reservation over 1,400+ nodes for a full day, so a 6-hour job submitted 1h37m before it opens waits ~22 hours instead of starting.

The skill made this worse than silent: its one mention of `ReqNodeNotAvail` (`slurm.md`) gave the single cause that was *not* responsible, "the partition lacks what was asked", sending a reader off to check GPU models.

## Changes

**`orcd_submit.py`** — detection where the decision is made:

- `--plan` and submit fetch reservations together with the **cluster's own clock** (the baseline Slurm compares against, which need not match the caller's), and name any window the requested `-t` would cross, with the largest walltime that still starts now and the `EndTime` to submit after.
- Only `MAINT`/`ALL_NODES` reservations and ones naming the target partition are reported; node-specific reservations (e.g. a 9-node `SPEC_NODES` hold) cannot be evaluated from here and are skipped, so it does not cry wolf.
- `--queue` explains a reservation-held row instead of printing `%R` uninterpreted.
- `parse_walltime` covers every sbatch `-t` form, including that bare `30` means thirty *minutes*.

```
WARNING: reservation monthly_maint starts 2026-09-15T00:00:00 (ends 2026-09-15T21:00:00, 1411 nodes, flags MAINT,SPEC_NODES,ALL_NODES).
A -t 6:00:00 request cannot finish before then, so Slurm holds it until the
window ends -- shown only as PENDING, reason `ReqNodeNotAvail, Reserved for
maintenance`, indistinguishable from ordinary queueing.
Largest walltime that starts now: -t 1:37:00 (97 min).
Otherwise submit after 2026-09-15T21:00:00.
```

**`orcd_snapshot.py`**: reservations are captured, printed in the summary and diffed, with a `significance()` note. A newly scheduled window becomes visible drift rather than a surprise, which is what that script exists for.

**Docs**: new "Reservations hold jobs silently" section in `slurm.md` with the fit arithmetic and `squeue -j <id> -o "%i %T %r"` (`%R` truncates the reason); the `ReqNodeNotAvail` gloss now gives both causes and how to tell them apart. `SKILL.md` gains one troubleshooting row and a clause under `--plan`.

## Testing

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: all pass. Nine new tests with fixtures from the observed window: every `-t` form, the 6-hour request caught with `-t 1:37:00` offered, a 1h30m request correctly *not* flagged, node-specific reservations ignored unless they name the partition, no guess without a walltime or cluster clock, the `--queue` hint firing only on a reservation hold, and the snapshot capture plus `significance()`.
- End-to-end smoke of `main()` with a stubbed cluster reproducing the scenario: `WOULD START` lands post-maintenance and the warning computes 1h37m.
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all 11 skills valid; every script's `--help` parses.

response.title: Extend StructSense skills resource extraction component to support the Resources Catalog use case
response.body:
@puja-trivedi @djarecka  The current implementation may not extract all the information required to represent resources in the BrainKB Resources Catalog.

Extend the extraction pipeline to support the use case described in [[Epic 02 — Resources Catalog](https://github.com/sensein/brainkbdocs/blob/design_doc/design/brainkb-architecture.md#epic-02---resources-catalog)](https://github.com/sensein/brainkbdocs/blob/design_doc/design/brainkb-architecture.md#epic-02---resources-catalog).

### Scope

Support extracting structured information for resource types such as:

* Datasets
* Tools and software
* Models
* Pipelines
* Archives
* Schemas
* Ontologies

Where available, extract:

* Stable identifiers and resource type
* Name and description
* Tasks, modalities, species, and topics
* Applicability conditions
* Benchmark evidence and usage examples
* Known limitations and failure modes
* Owners or maintainers
* Versions
* Expected inputs and outputs
* Source and provenance information

### Acceptance criteria

* The extraction output can represent each supported resource as a first-class entity.
* Extracted fields align with the resource entity schemas.
* Applicability conditions, benchmark evidence, failure modes, and provenance are captured when present in the source.
* Tool-specific metadata—including versions, owners, inputs, and outputs—is captured when available.
* Existing extraction behavior remains backward compatible.
* Tests or fixtures demonstrate extraction across multiple resource types.

response.title: Add Extraction Core LinkML schema for unified extraction records
response.body:
## Summary

Introduces the Extraction Core schema, a comprehensive LinkML model that provides a unified structure for all extracted records across the repository's skills (NER, relations, resources, assertions, evidence, etc.). The schema ensures reproducibility by capturing complete provenance information for every extracted item.

## Key Changes

- **New LinkML schema** (`schemas/extraction_core/extraction_core.yaml`): 
  - Defines `ExtractionRecord` as the abstract parent for all extracted items, with universal slots for source location, assertion text, and provenance
  - Includes 30+ concrete classes covering entities, mentions, assertions, evidence, relations, and resources
  - Maps to standard ontologies (Assertion-Evidence, StructSense NER, PROV-O, PAV, SEPIO, SKOS) for semantic interoperability
  - Captures complete extraction run metadata: skill version, model version(s), prompt hashes, configuration hashes, software versions, and ontology versions

- **Validation tooling** (`schemas/extraction_core/check_dataset.py`):
  - Validates datasets against the schema using LinkML
  - Enforces cross-record integrity rules: all references resolve, extracted_by models are in the run's models, accepted mappings meet quality criteria, etc.
  - Supports both YAML and JSON input

- **Documentation and examples**:
  - `README.md` explaining the schema design, universal slots, and usage patterns
  - Valid example dataset (`ExtractionDataset-hu2026.yaml`) demonstrating a complete NER + judging run
  - Invalid examples showing common errors (missing provenance, broken references)

- **Tests** (`tests/test_extraction_core.py`):
  - Validates schema loads correctly
  - Confirms all `ExtractionRecord` subclasses carry universal slots
  - Tests valid and invalid examples
  - Skipped gracefully if LinkML is not installed

- **CI integration** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):
  - New "Extraction Core schema" job that installs LinkML and runs schema tests

## Notable Design Decisions

- **Deterministic IDs**: All record IDs are deterministic CURIEs so re-running a pipeline doesn't mint new IDs for unchanged records
- **Reified relations**: Evidence-assertion and assertion-assertion relationships are separate classes so judges and humans can disagree without overwriting extractions
- **Content hashing**: Prompts and configurations are identified by SHA256 hashes, making the exact inputs recoverable even after files are edited
- **Multivalued source locations**: Records can be grounded in multiple sentences/spans (e.g., a relation supported by two mentions)
- **Flexible confidence**: Confidence is producer-reported and may not be a probability; `confidence_method` documents how it was computed

response.title: bkbit skill
Add neuroimaging-kg skill: build, join, validate and query neuroimaging knowledge graphs (with ABIDE demo and WikiSkill evolution)
response.body:
## What and why

Michelle asked for a clear demo of how a user could build a knowledge graph like the one shown in the ReproNim talk. No existing skill builds a dataset-level NIDM/PROV graph, joins it to other labs' graphs, checks it and queries it, so this adds **`neuroimaging-kg`**. It orchestrates existing tools and skills rather than re-implementing them:

- **PyNIDM** (`csv2nidm`, `bidsmri2nidm`) for the NIDM dataset layer (Neuroimaging Data Model: participants, measurements, derivatives), and PyNIDM's LinkML schema → SHACL via `linkml gen-shacl`
- **ReproNim** NIDM files and tool definitions (simple2_NIDM_examples, segstats_jsonld, ants/fsl_seg_to_nidm), and the ReproPond/ReproLake sharing model
- **`structsense`** (claims with evidence spans), **`synthscholar`** (systematic reviews as SLR Turtle), **`brainkb`** (publish)
- **Oxigraph** for SPARQL over named graphs

## What is in the skill

- `SKILL.md`: a 9-step workflow, each step naming the tool to call and the check that gates it, plus a "Before you start" section learned from rollouts.
- `scripts/`, all `uv run`-able with inline dependencies and tested on an offline fixture:
  - `record_activity.py` — PROV for an analysis step; files identified by SHA-256; AI agents recorded with their model id.
  - `join_identity.py` — reviewable identity links (never `owl:sameAs`), with conflict checks by concept or source variable and per-check comparison counts.
  - `validate_graph.py` — core SHACL shapes plus a mutation test: a deleted derivation edge must be caught.
  - `query_graph.py` — named graphs in Oxigraph; competency queries compared with gold answers.
  - `nidm_volumes.py` — brain volumes from ReproNim NIDM, joining the values in site files with the meanings in the tool CDE files, selected by unit.
  - `compare_graphs.py` — harmonising graphs from different contributors (see below).
- `references/`: modeling snippets, pitfalls, competency-question templates. `assets/core_shapes.ttl`.
- `examples/abide_one_site/`: a runnable demo for one ABIDE I site from pinned, hash-checked public files.
- `examples/claude_code_demo.md`: a copy-paste terminal demo (four prompts), tested headlessly.
- `wiki/`: a WikiSkill knowledge wiki and harness (below).

## Demo — actual output (`run_demo.sh Caltech`, 15 s after the first download)

```
PASS  Q1_participants                   38 in phenotype table, 38 linked to ReproNim's NIDM (age/sex/diagnosis agree)
PASS  Q2_cohort_by_diagnosis            mean FD < 0.2 mm: 19 autism / 19 control
PASS  Q3_fiq_and_freesurfer_hippocampus FIQ + FreeSurfer hippocampal volume: 18 / 19 (one missing FIQ)
PASS  Q4_cohort_provenance              step, software+version, parameter 0.2, input file + SHA-256
PASS  Q5_claims_using_dataset           Abraham 2017: predictive, 871 participants, 0.67, verbatim quote
      Q6_hippocampus_by_tool            participant 51456 left hippocampus: FSL 3,766 mm³ vs FreeSurfer 4,513.9 mm³
```

The mutation test deletes 11 derivation edges and the check catches it. Gold answers are computed from the source files, not from the store.

## Claude Code terminal demo (headless test, one continued session)

| Prompt | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Build + validate + load Caltech; explain in plain words | 34 s | correct summary; one slip: said three tools; Caltech has FreeSurfer and FSL only |
| 2. FIQ + FreeSurfer hippocampal volume by group, with SPARQL | 14 s | 18 / 19 |
| 3. Trace 51456's left-hippocampus volume to scan and software | 162 s | correct chain; finds that "FreeSurfer ran on this scan" is **not** recorded, only implied by the subject ID in the command line |
| 4. Who is excluded at mean FD < 0.15 mm, and what depends on them | 55 s | 51456 and 51469 → 17 / 19; flags two queries that ignore the cohort |

The full transcript is in `examples/claude_code_demo_transcript.md`.

## Skill evolution with WikiSkill

The skill was refined with WikiSkill (Tang et al., *WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution*, arXiv:2608.27454v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.27454v1):

- **Layers:** raw experience (trimmed rollout notes) → a persistent wiki of patterns → skill updates.
- **Gate:** each update is accepted only if held-out validation improves.
- **Rollouts:** isolated headless Claude Code (Sonnet), with the skill installed **without** its wiki.
- **Tasks:** 6 training and 3 validation tasks, with deterministic checkers whose gold comes from the pinned sources.
- **Baseline v0:** train 5/6, validation 4/6 (median 106.5 s).
- **Candidate v1** (built from 9 wiki patterns: locate the skill's files; run Python through uv; reuse the demo for pinned sites; persistent identifiers; NIDM volume structure + `nidm_volumes.py`; write Turtle safely): validation 5/6 (median 78.5 s). **Accepted.** The gain is one V2 run out of two and may be noise.
- **Deviations from the paper** (listed in `wiki/evolution_log.md`): one iteration, two replicates per validation task, one author agent acting as both maintainer and proposer, trimmed traces.
- **Open item:** a byte-order mark in a CSV header breaks `join_identity.py`. It was seen only in a validation trace, so it was deliberately not fixed here, to avoid leaking validation data into the skill.

## Harmonising graphs from different contributors (added after review)

New step 5b and `scripts/compare_graphs.py`. Each contributor's graph stays separate and is attributed with PROV; nothing is merged or overwritten. For each pair of contributors it reports:

1. **Identifier overlap:** participants (`ndar:src_subject_id` or a given key), datasets (IRI plus version) and publications (DOI), each as matched / only-A / only-B.
2. **Vocabulary alignment:** concepts the two share, plus elements with no shared concept. Those become proposed `skos:exactMatch`/`closeMatch` mappings in a review file. Nothing is asserted, and never `owl:sameAs`.
3. **Conflicts:** the same participant and concept with values outside a tolerance, flagged when units or labels differ (the "CSF" total-vs-ventricles ~200× case), and same-named cohorts with different members.

Output is JSON plus Markdown. The offline tests use two synthetic contributors with an ID mismatch, a concept mismatch, a value conflict and the 200× definition mismatch.

The one-site demo gains step 10, comparing our Caltech graph with ReproNim's as two contributors:
- all 38 of 38 participants match;
- 12 concepts are shared;
- 28 subscores have no shared concept but the same source variable, so they are proposed for review;
- 282 participant × concept values were compared and 0 conflict, as expected since both come from the same ABIDE table.

## Tests

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 161 OK (neuroimaging-kg tests skip without their dependencies).
- `tests.test_neuroimaging_kg` with rdflib, pyshacl and pyoxigraph: 17 OK. A new CI job installs these packages and runs it.
- `scripts/validate_skills.py`: all 12 skills valid. The installer dry run is OK.

## Limitations

- The demo covers one site and the phenotype + structural layers. Connectivity and analysis layers are described in the skill but not demonstrated.
- PyNIDM's own `csv2nidm` output does not conform to PyNIDM's LinkML schema (176 results). This is reported as a finding, not a gate.
- WikiSkill was run small: one iteration and a handful of tasks; it is not a benchmark.
- Answers from agents can still contain factual slips (see prompt 1). The skill's checks catch structural errors, not every statement.

response.title: synthscholar: search-to-review with the closure-mode PubMed search strategy
response.body:
### Summary
- Adds **Mode 4, search-to-review**: research question → reproducible MeSH-grounded PubMed query → all matching records → title/abstract screening → the existing Mode 3 review.
- Requires **no API key**: the host agent answers the model prompts. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is used only when the scripts run standalone.
- Builds the **MeSH index automatically** on first use (one-time download of ~120 MB).
- Based on current `main` (includes #47). Supersedes the earlier version of this PR, which copied the engine unchanged.
- Hybrid mode dropped, can be retrieved if necessary.

### Review comments and resolution
| Comment | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Build the MeSH index automatically | The index is downloaded, built directly from the compressed dump (the 2 GB `.nt` file is not written), validated (≥ 30,000 descriptors) and removed on failure. `--ensure-index` runs this step in advance; `SKILL.md` instructs the agent to run it. |
| Integrate rather than copy | Compared with the first version of this PR, about 900 lines are removed: web-app async code, `hybrid` mode, slot merging and the `llm` v1 prompt. Remaining modes: `closure` (default), `llm` (v2, for comparison) and `mesh_only`. |
| Consistency with search-strategy-generator | Query hashes are identical in all tested cases (Evaluation 1). |
| Article retrieval and review quality | A complete review was run end to end (Evaluation 2). |
| Code Reviewer agent | Review run; findings addressed; follow-up verdict *approve with suggestions* (Code review). |

### Changes
**Search strategy:** `scripts/generate_search_strategy.py`, `scripts/search_strategy/`
- Closure mode: the model marks concept spans in the question (k samples, majority vote); vocabulary is resolved from the local MeSH index.
- Agent-as-model flags, automatic index, and `--provenance-out search_provenance.json` (query, hash, date, filters, record count, and the source of the strategy).
- Output records `provider`, `model` and the voted spans; a failed segmentation is labelled as a fallback.

**Screening:** `scripts/screen_records.py` (new, standard library only)
- `plan` → batches decided by the agent or by parallel subagents → `status` → `apply`.
- Each decision is validated and logged with its reason. Output: a `corpus.json` in the format read by `fetch_ezproxy.py` and `run_local_review.py`, plus the PRISMA screening counts.

**Documentation:** `SKILL.md` (Mode 4 and agent rules), `references/search_strategy.md`, `README.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`.

**Tests:** 47 tests in `tests/test_synthscholar_*.py`; without a MeSH index (as on CI), 32 run and 15 are skipped.

**Fixes to existing scripts** (separate commits)
- `assemble_manuscript.py`: per-group summaries were rendered as raw Python dictionaries.
- Installation note: `prisma-review-agent` is not reachable, and `synthscholar` `main` lacks the required provenance fields; the documentation now points to `sensein/synthscholar` @ `improve_verification`.
- `run_local_review.py`: corpora built from the PubMed search are no longer labelled as user-supplied PDFs.

Modes 1–3 are otherwise unchanged.

### Evaluation 1: consistency with search-strategy-generator (`d79cdcf`, MeSH 2026)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Identical model answers given to both engines (60 cases: `mesh_only`, closure, `llm`) | 60/60 identical query hashes, re-checked after each commit |
| Prompts sent to the model | Byte-identical |
| Closure with Claude Haiku via OpenRouter (6 questions × 3 runs) | Same query in every run |
| Closure with Codex/GPT as the model (6 × 3) | 17 of 18 runs produce the same query as Haiku |
| Closure with Claude Code as the model, no key (2 questions) | Matches the baseline |
| `llm` mode | Queries vary between runs; two runs returned 0 records |

### Evaluation 2: end-to-end review on merged `main` 

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Search → screening | 78 records → 57 excluded, with reasons → 21 retained |
| Full text (open access) | 2 of 21 retrieved (20 had a DOI) |
| Eligibility → inclusion | 16 excluded → 5 studies (583 participants) |
| Export, writing check, citation check, manuscript gates | Valid; 0 issues; 5/5 citations verified; 0 failures |
| PDF | 15 pages (see follow-up 3) |

Retrieval was limited to OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar (no Unpaywall, PubMed Central or institutional access); 19 of 21 reports were therefore assessed on the abstract. The test evaluates the pipeline, not the conclusions of the review.

### Code review
`code-reviewer` agent (claude-code-templates), full diff:
- Initial review: 0 critical, 2 high, 4 medium, 8 low findings.
- All findings that do not alter queries are fixed and covered by tests: fallback provenance, error handling with distinct exit codes, index build cleanup, screening input validation, and tests for date slicing.
- Follow-up review: all in-scope findings resolved; verdict *approve with suggestions*.

### Follow-ups (outside this PR)
1. **Engine search quality** (from the code review). These changes alter queries and are proposed for search-strategy-generator first, then synced, so the two remain identical:
   - `strict_terms` truncation drops a heading's own synonyms (high);
   - unrelated headings within one span are combined with OR;
   - descendant headings add off-topic free-text terms;
   - inverted entry terms trigger PubMed `quotedphrasesnotfound` warnings.
2. **PubMed Central is absent from the open-access chain.** In Evaluation 2 it would have supplied 4 of the 19 missing full texts. The SynthScholar application includes this route; `oa_client.py` does not.
3. **`generate_review_pdf.py` fails on Windows with typst**, which rejects absolute `C:/` image paths. Pre-existing; PDFs build with TeX or with a two-step pandoc → typst conversion.
4. Optional: write fetched date slices to disk as they complete, for searches above 10,000 records.

### Testing
```bash
python -m unittest tests.test_synthscholar_search_strategy tests.test_synthscholar_manuscript
python scripts/validate_skills.py
python skills/synthscholar/scripts/generate_search_strategy.py --ensure-index
python skills/synthscholar/scripts/generate_search_strategy.py "<question>" --emit-prompt
```

**Files** (`trusted_ontologies/`, made with bkbit `ait2jsonld` from brain-bican/bkbit main `df56a65`, read from the released AIT `.h5ad` files):

| Manifest entry | `trusted_files` |

| Human MTG SMART-Seq (AIT15.3) | human: `Human_MTG.ttl` |
